question: What is a Kafka consumer group?
options: A set of brokers that replicate the same partition
A group of consumers that cooperate to consume a topic, with each partition read by only one member
A collection of topics grouped under a single namespace
A tool that monitors producer throughput
explanation: A consumer group is a set of consumers sharing a group.id that jointly consume a topic. Kafka assigns each partition to exactly one consumer in the group, enabling parallel, scalable consumption.

question: If a topic has 4 partitions and a consumer group has 6 consumers, what happens?
options: All 6 consumers each read all 4 partitions simultaneously
Kafka automatically creates 2 more partitions to match the consumers
The extra consumers throw errors and crash
4 consumers each get one partition and 2 consumers remain idle
explanation: A partition can be assigned to at most one consumer within a group. With more consumers than partitions, the surplus consumers sit idle until partitions free up or more are added.

question: How can two separate applications both receive every message from the same topic?
options: By putting each application in its own consumer group with a different group.id
By having both applications share a single group.id
By configuring the topic to duplicate every message
It is impossible; only one application can ever consume a topic
explanation: Each consumer group maintains its own offsets, so different groups independently receive all messages. Sharing a single group.id would split the messages between them instead.

question: What triggers a consumer group rebalance?
options: A producer increasing its batch size
A change in group membership, such as a consumer joining or leaving the group
A broker compressing log segments
A schema being registered in the Schema Registry
explanation: Rebalancing redistributes partitions among consumers when membership changes (a consumer joins, leaves, or fails) or when the subscribed topics' partitions change.

question: How do consumer groups enable horizontal scaling of message processing?
options: By compressing messages so they take less time to process
By caching all messages in memory across the group
By adding more consumers so partitions are spread across them, increasing parallelism
By reducing the topic's replication factor to speed up reads
explanation: Adding consumers (up to the number of partitions) distributes partitions across more processes, increasing parallel processing throughput. Beyond the partition count, extra consumers add no parallelism.
